extracted.intended_audience: NIH fellowship applicants, sponsors/mentors, and NIH peer reviewers
extracted.subtask_description: Official NIH guidance describing the restructured scored review criteria (effective for due dates on/after Jan 25, 2025) used to evaluate fellowship (F30, F31, F32, F33, F99/K00) applications, with explanatory guidance for reviewers and implications for applicants and sponsors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Candidate’s Preparedness and Potential
rubrics_metrics.description: Discuss the candidate’s preparedness for the proposed research training plan. Consider the context, for example, the candidate’s stage of training and the opportunities available. Assess whether the candidate and sponsor statements as well as the referee letters provide convincing evidence that the candidate possesses qualities (such as scientific understanding, creativity, curiosity, resourcefulness, and drive) that will improve the likelihood of a successful research training outcome. Consider the candidate’s potential to benefit from the fellowship research training plan and to transition to the next career stage in the biomedical research workforce.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate preparedness in context (stage of training, opportunities available). Look for convincing evidence across candidate statement, sponsor statement, and reference letters that the candidate has research-relevant qualities (scientific understanding, creativity, curiosity, resourcefulness, drive). Consider both the likelihood the candidate will benefit from the training plan and their potential to transition to the next career stage. Use these factors to assign a scored rating (1–9).

rubrics_metrics.name: Research Training Plan
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess the rigor and feasibility of the research training project and how completion of the project will contribute to the development of the candidate as a research scientist. Evaluate the goals of the overall research training plan and the extent to which the plan will facilitate the attainment of the goals. Discuss whether the research training plan identifies areas of needed development and contains appropriate, realistic activities and milestones to address those needs. Consider whether the sponsor(s), scientific environment, facilities, and resources are adequate and appropriate for the proposed research training plan.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judge both scientific rigor and training value: is the project feasible and rigorous, and will it materially develop the candidate? Look for clearly articulated goals, identified gaps in the candidate’s skills/knowledge, and realistic activities/milestones to fill those gaps. Evaluate adequacy/appropriateness of sponsor(s), environment, facilities, and resources in enabling the plan. Consider alignment between training activities and stated development goals when scoring (1–9).

rubrics_metrics.name: Commitment to Candidate
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess whether the sponsor(s) presents a strong mentoring plan appropriate to the needs and goals of the candidate. Evaluate the extent to which the sponsor(s) and organizational commitment is appropriate, sufficient, and in alignment with the candidate’s research training plan. Consider whether the level of commitment provided will contribute to the successful completion of the proposed plan and allow the candidate to advance to a productive career in the biomedical research workforce.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Look for a sponsor-provided mentoring plan tailored to the candidate’s needs and goals, and for demonstrable organizational support that aligns with the training plan. Consider whether sponsor time, mentorship activities, and institutional commitments (e.g., protected time, access to resources, career development opportunities) are sufficient to enable successful completion and career progression. Factor these elements into the scored review (1–9).

rubrics_metrics.name: Scoring framework for fellowship review criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: The revised fellowship peer review criteria are reorganized into three scored review criteria (Candidate’s Preparedness and Potential; Research Training Plan; Commitment to Candidate), each scored 1–9.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers assign a numeric score (1 = highest quality through 9 = lowest) to each of the three criteria. Use the descriptive guidance under each criterion to inform scoring. The restructured scoring is intended to focus evaluation on candidate potential and training plan quality rather than sponsor/institution reputation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Guiding principle: focus on candidate and targeted training needs
rubrics_metrics.description: The revision is intended to help reviewers better evaluate a candidate’s potential and the quality of their research training plan without the undue influence of the sponsor’s or institution’s reputation, and ensure that the information provided in the application is targeted to the fellowship candidate’s specific training needs and is aligned with restructured review criteria.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When preparing applications, sponsors and candidates should tailor statements and plans to the candidate’s specific training needs; reviewers should avoid allowing sponsor or institutional reputation to unduly influence judgments. Applications should provide information that is directly relevant to the candidate’s preparedness, the rigor/feasibility of the training plan, and concrete commitments to the candidate.
